headline_hook: Thinking Machines Drops 975B Open-Weights Inkling While Willison Exposes Claude's Fetch Blindspot
preview_topics: a web-fetch exfiltration attack on Claude tools
Fable 5 earning production trust at Base44

pick_of_the_day.thesis: Willison's exfiltration demo proves the AI security perimeter has already shifted from model alignment to tool configuration — most builders are still defending the wrong layer, and the fix isn't better guardrails but smaller permission surfaces.

model_literacy.relevance: Today's exfiltration attack exploits web-fetch permissions, not the model itself. As agents gain more tools (file access, code execution, web browsing), the attack surface is the union of all tool capabilities — understanding which tools can read sensitive data AND reach the network is the new security audit.

items.title: Thinking Machines Drops Inkling: 975B Open-Weights, Day-One HuggingFace Support
items.angle: A 975B MoE model with 41B active params, open-weights, and already in Transformers v5.14 on launch day — the open-model ecosystem now moves at parity speed with closed labs
items.key_fact: 975B total / 41B active parameters, Mixture-of-Experts, multimodal, integrated into HuggingFace Transformers on day one

items.title: HuggingFace Transformers v5.14.0 Ships Same-Day Inkling Support
items.angle: The de facto model integration layer adds Inkling support on launch day — if your model isn't in Transformers, it doesn't exist for most developers
items.key_fact: v5.14.0 release with native Inkling support plus multi-model updates

items.title: Claude Code Patches Bidi-Override Permission Spoof, Adds Screen Reader Mode
items.angle: Three releases in two days: a security fix for bidirectional-override characters that could spoof permission previews, plus accessibility and streaming improvements — the kind of quiet security work that matters most
items.key_fact: Security fix: bidirectional-override characters could disguise tool calls in permission dialogs

items.title: deja-vu: Zero-Dep Memory Layer for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode
items.angle: A single binary that adds persistent memory and secret redaction across coding agents — solves 'my agent forgot yesterday' without changing your workflow
items.key_fact: 189 GitHub stars, supports MCP recall, works across Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode

items.title: llama.cpp Gets CUDA Lightning Indexer for Faster NVIDIA Inference
items.angle: A dedicated CUDA kernel with generic vector and WMMA paths — the local inference stack keeps closing the gap with cloud APIs
items.key_fact: New Lightning Indexer kernel; b10034 also works around Adreno GPU MoE bugs on mobile

items.title: Simon Willison Demonstrates Web-Fetch Data Exfiltration Against Claude
items.angle: The attack isn't a jailbreak — it exploits the tool configuration layer, proving that AI security audits need to focus on which tools can read sensitive data AND reach the network simultaneously
items.key_fact: Data exfiltration via web-fetch tool; attack surface is tool permissions, not model alignment

items.title: IBM Research: Model Routing Gets Hard When Model Tiers Multiply
items.angle: As every provider ships 3-5 model tiers, routing becomes a real engineering problem — IBM's analysis shows it's not just a cost toggle anymore
items.key_fact: Routing complexity grows non-linearly with model tiers (GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Orbit, Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku)

items.title: What Allen AI Learned Building Shippy: An Agent Post-Mortem
items.angle: Hard-won lessons from a real agent deployment — what worked, what didn't, and why the agent-building community needs more experience reports like this
items.key_fact: Post-mortem from Allen AI's Shippy agent system covering practical failure modes

items.title: LLMs Meet MikroTik: Network Config Automation Where You Least Expect It
items.angle: A hands-on guide proving LLMs can handle niche infrastructure domains — network router config is the kind of 'long tail' use case that scales quietly
items.key_fact: Practical walkthrough of LLM-driven MikroTik router configuration and troubleshooting

items.title: Base44 Joins the Fable 5 Production Club — A Pattern Is Forming
items.angle: After Cognition, Base44 publicly documents trusting Fable 5 for their hardest engineering work — two case studies in a week signals agentic coding at scale is crossing the credibility threshold
items.key_fact: Second public case study of Fable 5 in production engineering after Cognition

items.title: lobste.rs Migrates to SQLite — Another High-Profile Validation
items.angle: The tech forum joins a growing list of production SQLite adopters — for AI developers running inference services, SQLite's operational simplicity is getting harder to argue against
items.key_fact: lobste.rs now runs on SQLite in production, following Litestream and Turso adoptions

items.title: QuantumByte: Describe What You Want, Get a Running App
items.angle: An open-source engine that goes from natural-language intent to working application — 310 stars and climbing in the intent-to-app space

items.title: Java Gets Native Local LLM Inference via Panama FFM — No JNI Required

items.key_fact: Uses OpenJDK Java 22 Panama FFM API, zero JNI or native wrapper overhead
